hypothesis: This package is corpus scaffolding, not an experiment. It fetches and caches the eighteenth-century chemistry documents named for Case 3 of the multi-case retrospective test in papers/dynamics_of_conceptual_deletion/paper.md (Lavoisier / phlogiston, 1783-1789). It makes no scientific claim; success is defined as every named Wikisource source fetching to substantive text.

controls.description: Every source is pulled through the same throttled Wikisource api.php pipeline used by experiments/date_cut_retrodiction/fetch.py; the container-extraction and chrome-removal logic is imported, not copied, so both corpora share provenance.
results/fetch_summary.json records the character count and SHA-256 of every cached document, so a re-fetch that silently produces different bytes is detectable.

Any cached document below 2000 characters is flagged as non-substantive in the summary. The one-off Fulhame 1789 'Letter to Joseph Black' fetched to 114 characters (cover-page only) and is excluded from corpus.SOURCES for that reason; the threshold catches any regression.

CORPUS_MANIFEST.md enumerates every author named in the paper (Stahl, Priestley, Cavendish, Scheele, Kirwan, Black, Hales, Fulhame) that is absent, with the specific reason (no author page, empty author page, scan-only Index, cover-page-only transclusion, or wrong-author reprint). No fabricated substitutes.

gates.criterion: Every SourceSpec in experiments.lavoisier_phlogiston_corpus.corpus.SOURCES fetches to a cached text file, and each cached file passes the 2000-character substantive-content threshold, as recorded in results/fetch_summary.json.
